newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh copper plant boosts H1 cathode output.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh copper plant boosts H1 cathode output.

text.p: Kazakhstan's largest copper maker Zhezkazgantsvetmet produced 105,000 tonnes of copper cathode in the first half of this year, 6.6 percent more than year-ago levels, the Industry Ministry said on Monday.
Boris Sadchikov, deputy head of the industry branches development section, also said Kazakhstan, which has other copper plants, was on track to boost total output this year.
"Most likely, Kazakhstan will produce 300,000-305,000 tonnes of copper this year," he said, up from 267,140 tonnes in 1996.
But the figure was still well below 1990's 365,000 tonnes.
Zhezkazgantsvetmet accounts for more than 60 percent of the ex-Soviet republic's copper output and produced 180,000 tonnes last year.

A report from the National Statistics Agency said total output of cathode copper in the Central Asian state fell in the first half of this year by seven percent to 140,300 tonnes from 150,900 tonnes in January-June of last year.
Zhezkazgantsvetmet is managed by South Korea's Samsung Corp unit Samsung Deutschland GmBH. Samsung has a 40 percent stake in the facility, in which it has invested $200 million.
Twenty percent of shares belong to workers. The government -- represented by the finance ministry's state property department -- holds 35 percent and investment funds hold the remaining five percemt.
Zhezkazgantsvetmet decided at its annual shareholders' meeting last week to pay a 10-tenge dividend per share, each nominally worth 20 tenge, a plant official said.
"The dividend is being paid on both ordinary and privileged shares," he said, adding Zhezkazgantsvetmet made a 1996 pre-tax profit of 8.0 million tenge.
